title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1968-12-20
lineage: SBD cassette master > cassette > DAT/0 > CDR/0 > CDR/1 > iMac > SHN

ai_review.summary: A fairly noisy audience recording with noticeable hiss captures a rare 1968 show highlighted by Mountains of the Moon and an inspired Lovelight.
ai_review.review: These reviews celebrate a historically significant 1968 performance – the first time the Dead played “Mountains of the Moon” and a memorable acoustic rendition by Jerry, plus Phil’s standout work on “Lovelight.” The tape suffers from hiss and occasional muffiness, but fans consider it worth the listen for the rare material.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is rated very high (rare songs, strong performances) while recording quality is modest due to hiss; combined weighted score yields ~4.1.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable tape hiss throughout; some sections require the volume to be turned up. Overall listenable but not crystal‑clear.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Dead folk style with typical pacing; the rarity of “Mountains of the Moon” and an acoustic guitar moment make the show feel special despite its modest overall flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Acoustic guitar on “Mountains of the Moon” noted as a very nice, rare moment.
